newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU PIG COUNT HIGHER DESPITE SWINE FEVER.
newsitem.headline: EU PIG COUNT HIGHER DESPITE SWINE FEVER.

text.p: Pig numbers in the European Union in April were up from a year ago as Dutch reductions were offset by livestock gains in other member states, the Bonn farm ministry said on Monday.
A total 116.9 million pigs were kept in the EU in April, compared with 115.0 million a year earlier, a report in its weekly circular said, citing the EU statistics office.
The numbers in the Netherlands and Belgium were lower at 13.2 (13.8) million and 6.6 (7.1) million respectively because of mass slaughterings after the outbreak of swine fever.

Dutch and Belgian slaughter pig supplies should be down by 30 percent and this would cause an overall reduction in EU pork production by two percent, although nearly all countries outside the two should show gains in output.
This should keep pork prices high, especially because the EU would be able to export to Japan, the ministry said.
Japan no longer imports supplies from Taiwan due to an outbreak of foot and mouth disease.
Germany's pig inventories rose to 24.4 million (from 23.6 million a year earlier), France's to 15.4 million (14.9) and Denmark's to 11.0 million (10.6).
